raw:
Professor Stone nods once.

“Food and clothes are practical questions. The Academy provides both. The rest of your inheritance will come with forms, invoices, and people claiming urgency. Read those more carefully.”

He slides the brown volume across the table. “Keep it until Thursday. Don’t write in it.”

For a while, the library gives you only lamp-oil, paper, and procedure. The first section describes the human seat less as a throne than a working office: recording consent in negotiations, carrying translations between delegations, and challenging terms that had not been fully explained. Nothing in it says a seat-holder must be a mage.

From the common room, Dena’s voice rises over a dispute about cards.

The library door opens. Seraphel steps in with a slim book tucked beneath one arm, pauses beside the table, and glances toward the noise.

“May I sit here?  
Their game has become  
more argument than cards.”
